talks: What’s New in Kairos, 2026 Edition; Cluster API in 15 Minutes. A Primer on Declarative Kubernetes Infrastructure; Verticalizing Platform Intelligence for Regulated Domains
bio:
William is a Kairos Maintainer, CNCF Ambassador and Linkerd Ambassador currently working at Mirantis as Global Field CTO. He’s focused on helping customers designing, building, and running their initiatives on Edge, AI and Platform Engineering. He wore many hats in the IT world, Engineering, Pre-Post sales, Product Owner and Consulting. from HPC, Storage to Distributed Systems.
William enjoys volunteering in several Cloud Native groups and organizing the KCD Netherlands events.

name: Wojciech Tyczyński
talks: The Scheduling Stack: Real-World Lessons from Anthropic, Anyscale, Google, and CERN
bio:
Wojciech is working on Google Technical Infrastructure & Cloud since 2012. Since 2015 he works on Kubernetes and GKE. With the main focus on scalability, performance and reliability, he gained experience and contributed to many Kubernetes features and most of its components. Currently his main focus is in the scheduling rea.
Before joining Google he graduated from University of Warsaw earning M.S. in Computer Science and B.S. in Mathematics.

name: Xing Yang
talks: Why Quotas Are Hard in Kubernetes: Lessons from Building a Production-Grade Quota System; Cloud Native Infrastructure in the AI Era: A TAG Infrastructure Panel; SIG Storage Intro and Deep Dive
bio: Xing Yang is a Tech Lead in the Cloud Native Storage team at VMware. She is a co-chair of CNCF Storage TAG, a co-chair of the Kubernetes Storage SIG, a co-chair of the Data Protection WG, and a maintainer in Kubernetes CSI. Before joining VMware, Xing was the Lead Architect of OpenSDS while working for Futurewei. She also worked at Dell EMC for many years and has developed deep expertise in storage, data protection, disaster recovery, cloud, and virtualization technologies.

name: Yair Temkin
talks: From Bearer Tokens to Mesh-Native mTLS: Modernizing Service Identity at Coinbase
bio: Yair Temkin is a software engineer on Coinbase's Compute Platform team, based in New York City, where he has spent two years working on service identity and Istio ambient mesh modernization across hundreds of Kubernetes services. He supported Coinbase's migration from a homegrown legacy bearer-token system to SPIFFE/SPIRE identities, and now owns the enforcement of service-to-service access through Istio AuthorizationPolicies and removal of per-pod auth sidecars via ztunnel mTLS.

name: Yan Avlasov
talks: Evolution of Agentic Networking Stack in Envoy
bio: Yan Avlasov is a senior maintainer of Envoy proxy. Yan works at Google, helping teams deploy Envoy based products and ensuring that Envoy and Envoy based products meet Google’s standards for safety and security.

name: Yan Wang
talks: Securing the Agentic Future: Distributing LLM Weights and Sandboxed AI Agents via Harbor
bio: I am is a Staff engineer working on Broadcom. As one of the core maintainer of CNCF project Harbor and the maintainer of CNCF project distribution, I am main work focuses on technology research and innovation in the cloud native field.

name: Yaron Schneider
talks: Verifiable Execution: Durable Workflows That Cryptographically Prove What They Did
bio: Yaron co-created the CNCF projects Dapr and KEDA while at Microsoft and led the engineering architecture for serverless container platforms that run at scale using open source technologies. Yaron is an avid lover of open source tech and distributed systems, and is a co-founder and CTO at Diagrid, a company focused on providing application developers with APIs and tools based on open source. When not maintaining the Dapr project, Yaron enjoys playing guitar, recording music and reading.

name: Yash Sharma
talks: Meshery: Your Cluster as a Knowledge Graph, Not a Pile of YAML; Following the Evidence with HolmesGPT: Troubleshooting Kubernetes Apps and Underlying Infrastructure; Meshery Contribfest: Ship Your First PR to a CNCF Cloud Native Manager
bio: Yash is Developer Advocate at UiPath, KubeCon speaker and a core maintainer of Meshery, an open-source CNCF sandbox project. He is a mentor for the LFX 2024 projects and was an LFX mentee in the 2023 mentorship under Meshery. He hosts weekly Meshery Development calls and engage in CNCF communities

name: Yashash Lokesh
talks: Millions of Events, One Right Order: Financial Data Processing at Intuit
bio: Yashash is a Software engineer for the Intuit Platform and Analytics team in Mountain View, California. He is one of the lead contributors to open source Numaproj streaming platform. His focus areas include stream processing, analytics and observability.

name: Yin Ding
talks: Fighting Fire with Fire: Scaling KubeEdge Vulnerability Management in the New AI Era
bio:
Yin Ding, an Engineering Leader at VMware, lead the Photon team and brings over 15 years of expertise in large-scale and distributed computing.
As a co-founder of the CNCF KubeEdge open-source project and the TSC Chair of LF Edge Akraino, Yin Ding has made significant contributions to the advancement of these platforms. He has also contributed to various other open-source projects, including Kubernetes, OpenStack, and Cloud Foundry.

name: Ying Xiong
job: Head of Data Infra @ Apple Maps
talks: Why We Bet the Data Platform on Kubernetes - And How AI Is Changing How We Operate It
bio: Head of Data Infra & OSS champion. Veteran in data, cloud & agentic AI.

name: Yiqing Wang
talks: Many Clusters, One GPU Pool: Locality-Aware Scheduling and Data Delivery With Kueue and Dragonfly
bio: Yiqing Wang is a tech lead on Roblox's ML Platform team, focused on distributed ML infrastructure and large-scale GPU systems. He builds multi-cluster platforms for training, reinforcement learning, batch inference, and LLM serving across cloud and on-premises environments. His work spans GPU scheduling and quota management with Kueue, RayJob orchestration with KubeRay, and high-performance data storage and delivery using shared file systems and CNCF Dragonfly.

name: Yodar Shafrir
talks: Demo Theater: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Kubernetes; Context Unlocks Autonomous AI Infrastructure

name: Yong Tang
talks: From Cloud Outages to AI Security Challenges: Building Resilient DNS Infrastructure at Scale
bio: Yong Tang is Senior Director of Engineering at Ivanti. He is a core maintainer of CoreDNS and contributes to many container, cloud-native, and machine learning projects for the open source community. In addition to CoreDNS, he is a maintainer of Docker/Moby. He is also a maintainer and SIG I/O lead of the TensorFlow project. Yong Tang has multiple talks in KubeCon in the past covering areas of service discovery, data processing, and machine learning.

name: Yoshiyuki Tabata
talks: One Platform for AuthN and AuthZ: Keycloak Meets AuthZEN
bio:
Yoshiyuki Tabata is an OSS consultant with over a decade of experience in IAM, API platforms, and cloud‑native security. He serves as Tech Lead of CNCF TAG Security and Compliance and is a Project Lead and author of the CNCF IAM Whitepaper. He is also a recipient of the 2026 CNCF TAGGIE Award.
He is a frequent speaker at global conferences such as KubeCon. In the Keycloak community, he has served as a co‑chair of KeycloakCon and supports community engagement through events.

name: Youmin Han
job: Staff Software Engineer @ Linkedin AI Platform
talks: Ship Faster, Ship Safer: A K8s-Native Canary Pipeline for Critical Cluster Services
bio: Staff Software Engineer at LinkedIn AI Platform Training team, working on Kubernetes-based ML infrastructure and large-scale training systems.

name: YoungJoon Jeong
talks: What the Docs Don't Tell You: A Telecom's Year Operating Cache-Aware LLM Inference on Kubernetes
bio: YoungJoon Jeong is a Specialist Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services (AWS), specializing in Kubernetes platform engineering and AI/ML infrastructure. He works with enterprises across the APJC region on production EKS deployments spanning agentic AI platforms, GPU scheduling, hybrid infrastructure, and security governance. He publishes an open-source engineering playbook covering EKS best practices, AI platform architecture, performance benchmarks, and cloud-native operations.

name: Yuan Chen
talks: One Recipe, Five Clouds, One Query: Portable GPU Configuration with a Queryable Audit Layer
bio: Yuan Chen is a Principal Software Engineer at NVIDIA, where he builds cloud-native Kubernetes infrastructure for AI. He previously built hyperscale Kubernetes infrastructure at Apple. Yuan has contributed to open source Kubernetes and the CNCF community and has delivered 14 KubeCon talks. He was previously a Principal Architect at JD.com and a Principal Researcher at Hewlett-Packard Labs. He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Georgia Tech.

name: Yuan Tang
job: Co-Founder at TensorScale AI; Project Lead at Argo, Kubeflow, and KServe
talks: Explore TAG Workloads Foundation: Core Runtime, Batch Scheduling, and Moar
bio: Co-founder at TensorScale AI, focusing on building AI stack for world models. He led AI infrastructure and platform teams at various companies, including Red Hat and Alibaba. He holds leadership roles in open source communities — including Argo, Kubeflow, KServe, Kubernetes, and CNCF — and maintains many open source projects. Yuan has authored award-winning books and highly cited papers and patents, and is a frequent keynote speaker, technical advisor, and mentor at various organizations.

name: Yuchen Zhou
talks: When Training Dies at 3 AM: Correlating Kubernetes Events with AI-Framework Failures
bio: Been at GKE for almost 7 years, working on different areas including both oss work, GKE internal operation systems and AI infra support.

name: Yue Bao
talks: Fighting Fire with Fire: Scaling KubeEdge Vulnerability Management in the New AI Era
bio: Yue Bao serves as a software engineer of Huawei Cloud. She is now working 100% on open source, focusing on lightweight edge and edge api-server for KubeEdge. Before that, Yue worked on Huawei Cloud Intelligent EdgeFabric Service and participated in multiple edge engineering projects. Yue graduated from Chu Kochen Honors College of Zhejiang University, majoring in information science and electronic engineering.

name: Yugo Kobayashi
talks: What's New with Kubectl and Kustomize … and How You Can Help!
bio:
He is a software engineer who focuses on building high-efficiency and usable internal platforms.
He's also the maintainer of kubernetes-sigs/kustomize.

name: Yuke Ning
talks: AI Gateways in Practice: Model Routing, Inference Scheduling, and MCP on Kubernetes
bio: Yuke Ning works at Alibaba Cloud, focusing on cloud native infrastructure and reliability. His interests include Kubernetes, AI infrastructure, and agent systems. He contributes to open source projects and enjoys sharing practical experience in building and operating reliable cloud native systems.

name: Yuki Iwai
talks: WG-Batch Updates: What’s New and What Is Next?
bio: Yuki is a Software Engineer at Preferred Networks, Inc. He works on the AI / ML / HPC Platform. He is currently a Lead for Kubernetes WG Batch and Kubeflow WG Training. He is also a kube-controller-manager Job reviewer, and a Kubernetes' Kueue Lead.

name: Yury Tsarev
talks: Crossplane Contribfest - Start Your Journey to Crossplane Function Maintainer
bio: Yury is an experienced software engineer who strongly focuses on open-source, software quality and distributed systems. As the creator of k8gb (https://www.k8gb.io) and active contributor to the Crossplane ecosystem, he frequently speaks at conferences covering topics such as Control Planes, GSLB, and the experience of running reliable and testable infrastructure at a huge scale. He enjoys his role in Upbound, helping organizations worldwide to revolutionize their infrastructure with Crossplane.

name: Yusheng Zheng
talks: Beyond Harnesses and Sandboxes: Runtime Protection for AI Agents with eBPF
bio: Yusheng Zheng is an OSS maintainer working on eBPF and AI Agents. As the founder of the eunomia-bpf community and currently a PhD student researching how to integrate eBPF with AI to improve the observability and programmability of modern software systems, including the Linux kernel, userspace applications, and GPUs, Yusheng frequently speaks at technical conferences such as KubeCon, LPC, and OSS Summit and discusses practical insights and the future roles of eBPF and AI in system design..

name: Yuva Peavler
talks: Follow the GPUs: How a Regulated Fortune 100 Serves Customers When No Single Cloud Has Enough
bio: Yuva Peavler is a Staff Engineer at GEICO, where she works on the Hybrid Cloud Compute platform team. She builds and operates the infrastructure that delivers Kubernetes clusters, service mesh, workload identity, and observability to internal teams.

name: Zachary Schwartz
talks: From Bearer Tokens to Mesh-Native mTLS: Modernizing Service Identity at Coinbase
bio: As a Software Engineer at Coinbase, I’m currently focused on expanding our service mesh capabilities, and specialize in cloud-native networking and secure infrastructure at scale. I am passionate about zero-trust security and service identity, bridging the gap between complex orchestration and seamless protection.

name: Zaira Shaikh
talks: Managing Network Security in Multi-Tenant Environments with Istio and Cilium
bio: Zaira works on the Hybrid Cloud Fabric team at GEICO Tech, working full-time with Istio, Cilium, OpenPolicyAgent, and Go. Outside of work she enjoys cooking, leatherworking, and tinkering with her many computers.

name: Zhang Zhen
talks: Demystifying Upgrades for Stateful, Dormant AI Agents: Unleashing Seamless Updates in Dynamic Sand
bio: Zhen Zhang has been working on the cluster management of software applications. he is driving the new cloud native innovation in Alibaba and focus mainly on the application management domain. He is one of main maintainer in OpenKruise project.

name: Zhewei Hu
talks: Breaking the O(n²) Wall: Pub/Sub Federation for Istio Multicluster Service Discovery
bio: Zhewei Hu is a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), specializing in service mesh technologies like Istio and Envoy. He is the co-owner of Envoy ZooKeeper proxy filter.

name: Zhuo Zhi
talks: Ship Faster, Ship Safer: A K8s-Native Canary Pipeline for Critical Cluster Services
bio: Zhuo is a Senior Software Engineer at LinkedIn, specializing in Kubernetes-based machine learning infrastructure. He has contributed significantly to LinkedIn’s Kubernetes-native ML training platform, collaborating across teams to optimize scheduling and improve system observability. Zhuo is passionate about distributed systems and making large-scale ML training efficient and reliable.

name: Zixuan Feng
talks: AI-DDoS: How AI-Generated Contributions Are Breaching OSS Communities, and What We Can Do about It
bio: Zixuan (Steve) Feng is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science at Virginia Commonwealth University. His research focuses on open-source software sustainability from a sociotechnical perspective. He directs the NOODLE Lab (Navigating Open-source, Organization, Developer, and Learning Ecosystems), which studies how people, communities, and AI systems shape the future of software development.

name: Zvonko Kaiser
talks: If It's Shared, It's Vulnerable: Is Kubernetes the Right Platform for Confidential Compute?
bio: Zvonko Kaiser is a Principal Systems Software Engineer at NVIDIA, specializing in cloud-native confidential computing and GPU security. He served on the Kata Containers Architecture Committee and serves on the Confidential Containers TSC, and chairs the Kubernetes WG AI Integration. As the primary architect behind Kata and Confidential Containers at NVIDIA, he hardens the cloud-native stack from silicon to service, guided by his principle that "if it's shared, it's vulnerable."
